text.p: Swiss Medical technology group Disetronic Holding AG said group net profit surged 88.2 percent to 24.5 million Swiss francs in the 1996/97 financial year, partially due to higher financial income.

Excluding the capital gains, which stem from investments of the Initial Public Offering (IPO) and other capital gains on sale of company stock, net profit would have risen 66.4 percent to 20.0 million francs.

Disetronic also said in a statement that its board would propose to shareholders on June 23 a dividend of four francs per bearer share. The payout only represents a quarterly dividend as Disetronic was not allowed to pay dividends until the end of the 1996 calender year under a special tax break agreement.

Sales in the 1996/97 financial year, which ended March 31, rose 24.0 percent to 102.4 million, the first time the company's sales topped the 100 million mark. Higher sales of insulin pumps and insulin pens were the main contributors to growth.

Operating profit rose 10.5 percent to 18.5 million francs, but the operating margin fell to 18.1 percent from 20.3 percent, partially due to a disproportionate increase in marketing and selling costs and one-time cost from the IPO last summer.
Disetronic said it would present its results on May 27.
